prompt:
You are the same engineer continuing your staged implementation.

SPECIFICATION:
Build a small Python 3 standard-library-only order processing system. It must work across multiple module boundaries and JSON snapshot/restore. Produce ledger.py, outbox.py, service.py, and HANDOFF.md. No network, filesystem writes, subprocesses, or external packages in candidate code. Deterministic caller-supplied time; no wall-clock calls.

ledger.py: Ledger(snapshot=None). apply(event) -> bool. event is exactly a dictionary with nonempty string id, order_id, kind and a positive integer amount (booleans are invalid). kind is reserve, capture, or refund. A reserve creates a new order and sets its reserved amount; a second reserve for the same order is invalid. Capture requires an existing order and cumulative capture <= reserved. Refund requires cumulative refund <= captured. All invalid events raise ValueError and change neither balances nor deduplication state. Reusing an event id with identical content returns False; reusing it with different content raises ValueError. An accepted new event returns True. balances(order_id) returns {reserved, captured, refunded, available, net}, with available=reserved-captured and net=captured-refunded; unknown order raises KeyError. snapshot() returns a JSON-serializable value. Constructor and snapshot must deep-copy their input/output.

outbox.py: Outbox(snapshot=None). enqueue(key, payload) -> bool: new nonempty string key returns True; same key and equal JSON payload returns False; same key different payload raises ValueError. Copy payloads, do not alias callers. claim(worker, now, lease) -> None or {key,payload,version}; worker must be a nonempty string and lease > 0, invalid inputs raise ValueError. Select the earliest-enqueued uncompleted item whose lease is absent or expired (now >= expiry). Each claim/reclaim increments that item's version. A completed item is never reissued. complete(key, worker, version, now) -> bool: only the current, unexpired owner with exact version may complete; all unknown/stale/wrong owner/already completed attempts return False without changes. snapshot() and constructor use JSON-serializable deep copies.

service.py: Service(snapshot=None) exposes ledger and outbox attributes, ingest(event) -> bool, dispatch(worker,now,lease,sink) -> bool, snapshot(). ingest applies one event and enqueues a notification with key event['id'] and payload equal to event. Duplicate events must not enqueue twice. If enqueue raises, roll back both ledger and outbox and re-raise. dispatch claims one item, calls sink(key,payload), then completes with exact owner/version at supplied now. No available item returns False; successful delivery and completion returns True. If sink raises, propagate and leave the lease outstanding. On expiry a retry is allowed. A process can die after the sink applies an effect but before completion: sink must implement durable idempotency by key; never promise exactly-once transport. Service.snapshot() covers both components. Restoration and snapshots must not alias live state.

HANDOFF.md: 120–220 words, for the engineer resuming this work. Explain module responsibilities, event-id idempotency, expiry/reclaim and stale-owner rejection, sink success-before-ack crash window, and the boundary of the in-memory transaction (a production database transaction is still needed). State limitations plainly. Do not claim the underlying queue alone gives exactly-once external effects. Do not invent test counts or performance claims.

All callers operate serially within one Service instance; thread-safe candidate internals are not required. Snapshot inputs are valid snapshots emitted by the matching class, possibly round-tripped through JSON. There are no hidden schema requirements for snapshot internals. Hidden tests exercise only the public behavior above. Return a JSON object with a files mapping from the requested names to their full contents. Additional prose outside JSON is tolerated by extraction, but files must parse and run.


YOUR STAGE:
Integrate the two implementations with service.py and HANDOFF.md. Resolve defects and interface mismatches. Return all four complete files in the files mapping.

{"architect": "```json\n{\n  \"plan\": \"**Module Interfaces & Invariants**\\n\\n*Ledger*: Maintains orders dict {order_id \u2192 {reserved, captured, refunded, event_ids: set}}. apply(event) validates required fields (nonempty string id/order_id/kind, positive int amount), enforces invariants (reserve only on new order, capture \u2264 reserved, refund \u2264 captured), then mutates. All validation failures raise ValueError without state change. snapshot() and __init__ deep-copy to prevent aliasing from caller mutations.\\n\\n*Outbox*: Maintains items dict {key \u2192 {payload (deep-copied), version: int, expiry: int|None, worker: str|None, completed: bool}}. enqueue(key, payload) returns True for new key, False for identical payload reuse, raises ValueError for same key + different payload. claim(worker, now, lease) selects earliest uncompleted item with absent/expired lease, increments version, sets expiry = now + lease, returns {key, payload, version} or None. complete(key, worker, version, now) succeeds only if item exists, not completed, worker matches current owner, version matches current, and now < expiry; sets completed=True. Returns False for stale/wrong owner/expired/unknown. snapshot()/constructor deep-copy.\\n\\n*Service*: Wraps ledger and outbox as attributes. ingest(event) applies event to ledger, then enqueues {key: event['id'], payload: event} to outbox. Returns False if no claim; True on successful complete. Provides event-id deduplication to support\\n    recovery and replay scenarios.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    \\n    def __init__(self, snapshot=None):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"Initialize ledger from an optional snapshot.\\n        \\n        Args:\\n            snapshot: Optional JSON-serializable snapshot dict from a prior\\n                     ledger.snapshot() call. Deep copy to prevent aliasing with caller's snapshot\\n            snapshot_copy = copy.deepcopy(snapshot)\\n            self._orders = snapshot_copy.get(\\\"orders\\\", {})\\n            self._event_history = snapshot_copy.get(\\\"event_history\\\", {})\\n    \\n    def apply(self, event):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"Apply an event (reserve, capture, or refund) to the ledger.\\n        \\n        Args:\\n            event: A dict with fields:\\n                - id (str, nonempty): unique event identifier\\n                - order_id (str, nonempty): which order this affects\\n                - kind (str): one of 'reserve', 'capture', 'refund'\\n                - amount (int, > 0): number of units (booleans rejected)\\n        \\n        Returns:\\n            True if event is new and successfully applied.\\n            False if event id was seen before with identical content.\\n        \\n        Raises:\\n            ValueError if event is invalid, violates invariants,\\n                       or reuses event id with different content.\\n                       No state changes occur on error.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        # Validate event is a dictionary\\n        if not isinstance(event, dict):\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"event must be a dict\\\")\\n        \\n        # Validate and extract required fields\\n        if \\\"id\\\" not in event:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"event missing required field 'id'\\\")\\n        event_id = event[\\\"id\\\"]\\n        if not isinstance(event_id, str) or not event_id:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"'id' must be a nonempty string\\\")\\n        \\n        if \\\"order_id\\\" not in event:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"event missing required field 'order_id'\\\")\\n        order_id = event[\\\"order_id\\\"]\\n        if not isinstance(order_id, str) or not order_id:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"'order_id' must be a nonempty string\\\")\\n        \\n        if \\\"kind\\\" not in event:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"event missing required field 'kind'\\\")\\n        kind = event[\\\"kind\\\"]\\n        if not isinstance(kind, str) or kind not in (\\\"reserve\\\", \\\"capture\\\", \\\"refund\\\"):\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"'kind' must be one of 'reserve', 'capture', 'refund'\\\")\\n        \\n        if \\\"amount\\\" not in event:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"event missing required field 'amount'\\\")\\n        amount = event[\\\"amount\\\"]\\n        # Deduplication: check if event_id was seen before\\n        if event_id in self._event_history:\\n            if self._event_history[event_id] == event:\\n                return False  # Identical event, already processed\\n            else:\\n                raise ValueError(\\\"event 'id' reused with different content\\\")\\n        \\n        # Supports multiple workers with version increments\\n    on reclaims.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    \\n    def __init__(self, snapshot=None):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"Initialize outbox from an optional snapshot.\\n        \\n        Args:\\n            snapshot: Optional JSON-serializable snapshot dict from a prior\\n                     outbox.snapshot() call. Input is deep-copied to prevent\\n                     aliasing with the caller's copy.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        if snapshot is None:\\n            self._items = {}  # {key: {payload, version, expiry, worker, completed}}\\n            self._insertion_order = []  # Track insertion order for claim()\\n        else:\\n            # Deep copy to prevent aliasing with caller's snapshot\\n            snapshot_copy = copy.deepcopy(snapshot)\\n            self._items = snapshot_copy.get(\\\"items\\\", {})\\n            self._insertion_order = snapshot_copy.get(\\\"insertion_order\\\", [])\\n    \\n    def enqueue(self, key, payload):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"Enqueue a notification with the given key and payload.\\n        \\n        Args:\\n            key: A nonempty string identifier (typically event['id'])\\n            payload: A JSON-serializable object (typically the event itself)\\n        \\n        Returns:\\n            True if key is new and successfully enqueued.\\n            False if the same key with identical payload already exists.\\n        \\n        Raises:\\n            ValueError if key is not a nonempty string or if the same key\\n                       exists with different payload.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        # Identical payload, already enqueued\\n            else:\\n                raise ValueError(\\\"key already exists with different payload\\\")\\n        \\n        # New key: add to outbox\\n        self._items[key] = {\\n            \\\"payload\\\": copy.deepcopy(payload),\\n            \\\"version\\\": 0,\\n            \\\"expiry\\\": None,\\n            \\\"worker\\\": None,\\n            \\\"completed\\\": False\\n        }\\n        self._insertion_order.append(key)\\n        return True\\n    \\n    def claim(self, worker, now, lease):\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"Claim an unclaimed or expired item for processing.\\n        \\n        Args:\\n            worker: A nonempty string identifying the claiming worker\\n            now: Current timestamp (integer)\\n            lease: Lease duration in time units (must be > 0)\\n        \\n        Returns:\\n            A dict {key, payload, version} for the claimed item,\\n            or None if no unclaimed/expired uncompleted item is available.\\n        \\n        Raises:\\n            ValueError if worker is not a nonempty string or lease <= 0.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        # Return the claimed item\\n                return {\\n                    \\\"key\\\": key,\\n                    \\\"payload\\\": copy.deepcopy(item[\\\"payload\\\"]),\\n                    \\\"version\\\": item[\\\"version\\\"]\\n                }\\n        \\n        return None  # Unknown key\\n        if key not in self._items:\\n            return False\\n        \\n        item = self._items[key]\\n        \\n        # Already completed\\n        if item[\\\"completed\\\"]:\\n            return False\\n        \\n        #
